title: mail-server MemoryBackend: Email mailboxIds may name a nonexistent Mailbox
description: Found by cyub.4 differential tests (testjig vs Stalwart). jmap-mail-server's MemoryBackend accepts an Email/set create or update whose mailboxIds names a Mailbox the account does not have, e.g. create {x:{mailboxIds:{"zz9-no-such":true},...}} succeeds, and update {<id>:{mailboxIds:{"zz9-no-such":true}}} succeeds. Stalwart answers invalidProperties ["mailboxIds"]. RFC 8621 §4.1.1: mailboxIds is the set of Mailbox ids the Email belongs to; §5.3 invalidProperties. Fix: check in create_email, copy_object, import_email_unchecked, and update_object when mailboxIds is patched (the cyub.4 agent wrote and reverted it). Blocker: it breaks ~125 existing jmap-mail-server tests in 9 files (mostly tests/integration.rs) that file Emails into a never-created 'inbox' Mailbox. Plan: first change the shared test fixtures to create the Mailboxes they use, land that, then the check; remove the KNOWN testjig entry in crate-jmap-interop/tests/differential.rs. Canonical template: same check in any sibling backend that stores Email-like mailbox membership.
close_reason: Email mailboxIds must name existing Mailboxes (create, update incl. patch, copy, import/deliver, create_object): invalidProperties [mailboxIds], after existence/permission per decision 44; fixtures now create the Mailboxes they use (122 tests, 11 files); 7 regression tests; differential testjig-bug entry removed, 23/23 live vs Stalwart
